design_rationale: The study is an open-label, multicentre, randomized controlled trial in which participants were randomly assigned (1:1) using a central, web-based random block design.

domain_judgments.rationale: The allocation sequence was generated using a central, web-based random block design, ensuring allocation was concealed until assignment, and baseline characteristics were balanced between groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The randomisation sequence was established before enrolment of the first patient and was done by use of a prespecified, secure, central, web-based randomisation system... Once a patient’s data were entered as meeting criteria for the study, including informed consent, the electronic enrolment system provided the site with the appropriate random treatment assignment...

domain_judgments.rationale: Although this was an open-label trial, analyses followed the intention-to-treat principle, and deviations from intended intervention were minimal (2 patients per group switched/did not receive assignment) with no indication of bias affecting outcomes.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary efficacy endpoint was the composite of all-cause hospitalisation and all-cause mortality at 21 days after randomisation and, in our main analysis, was analysed in the intention-to-treat population, which comprised all patients who were randomly assigned.

domain_judgments.rationale: Follow-up for the primary outcome at 21 days was available for nearly all participants (214 of 219 randomised, >97%), with minimal loss to follow-up balanced between groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: 111 with 21 days’ follow-up [standard of care, 3 with <21 days]; 103 with 21 days’ follow-up [enoxaparin, 2 with <21 days]

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcome (all-cause mortality and hospitalisation) was centrally adjudicated by an independent committee blinded to treatment assignment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary efficacy outcome and the bleeding events outcome were centrally adjudicated. Personal identifiers and treatment information were removed from all medical records before sharing the data with the Clinical Events Committee. The Clinical Events Committee were responsible for systematically adjudicating death, hospitalisation, and the classification of bleeding in a blinded way to the treatment assignment according to predefined clinical outcome definitions.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial had a registered protocol (NCT04492254), and the primary composite outcome and planned analyses were fully reported in accordance with the prespecified plan.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: This trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT04492254, and is complete... The primary outcome was the composite of all-cause death and all-cause admission to hospital (hospitalisation) at 21 days after randomisation... analysed in the intention-to-treat population...

overall_summary: The ETHIC randomized trial was conducted with appropriate central randomization, intention-to-treat analyses, low missing outcome data, blinded central outcome adjudication, and consistent reporting according to its registered trial protocol, resulting in low risk of bias across all RoB 2 domains.

design_rationale: The study is described as a phase 2b randomized trial where participants were randomized 1:1, stratified by site and symptom duration, to rivaroxaban or placebo.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants were randomized 1:1 using stratification, with balanced baseline characteristics across groups, and allocation was managed in a controlled trial framework.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Participants were randomized 1:1, stratified by site and symptom duration (<6 days vs ≥6 days), to receive either rivaroxaban (one 10-mg tablet) or placebo equivalent (multivitamin, 1 tablet) orally daily for 21 consecutive days.

domain_judgments.rationale: The study used a blinded placebo control, analysis was conducted on an intention-to-treat basis, and no trial-context deviations affecting intervention adherence were reported.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The intention-to-treat (ITT) population (all randomized participants) was used for the primary analysis after interactions with regulators.

domain_judgments.rationale: Early termination for futility and study dropouts resulted in missing day 28 outcome data for approximately 11% of the randomized ITT participants (analysis included 222 in each arm out of 246 and 251 randomized).
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The study was terminated after 497 of the target 600 participants were enrolled due to a prespecified interim analysis... At study termination (4 February 2021), 321 (65%) had already completed the study... The numbers of participants in each analysis population were similar between treatment groups (Figure 1).

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcomes were measured using standardized clinical scales, pulse oximetry, and temperature assessments in a double-blind setting where participants and assessors were blinded.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Through day 28, the investigator assessed COVID-19 signs and symptoms per checklist (Supplementary Materials 1), Gates Medical Research Institute (MRI) scale, and World Health Organization (WHO) scale (Supplementary Tables 2 and 3, respectively) as well as temperature and oxygen saturation measured by participants.

domain_judgments.rationale: Analyses followed a prespecified statistical analysis plan with group sequential interim monitoring boundaries and standard prespecified primary endpoints.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The final statistical analysis plan was amended to remove a second planned interim analysis after 67% of participants completed day 28, due to fast enrollment. The amendment also mitigated potential substantial underestimation of the treatment effect following early study termination and study drug termination of many of the enrolled participants at the time futility was declared.

overall_summary: The trial was a well-designed, randomized, placebo-controlled study, but early termination for futility led to missing primary outcome data for approximately 11% of randomized participants, raising some concerns for missing outcome data.

design_rationale: The study is an adaptive, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial where participants were centrally randomized 1:1:1:1 to one of four arms using computer-generated permuted blocks.

domain_judgments.rationale: Random sequence generation and allocation concealment were robustly implemented centrally via an electronic data-capture system with permuted blocks, and baseline characteristics were well balanced across groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Randomization code lists were computer generated using permuted blocks with block size equal to 4 during the process of drug labeling and then implemented electronically through the central electronic data-capture system.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was double-blind and placebo-controlled with identical administration, and both the modified intention-to-treat (treated) population and full intention-to-treat population across all randomized participants were analyzed with consistent results.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary sample of interest for both efficacy and safety treatment comparisons was defined on an a priori basis and consisted of all randomized participants who initiated trial therapy and had at least 1 follow-up assessment during the 45-day treatment period... Secondary efficacy and safety analyses were conducted among all randomized participants according to assigned treatment

domain_judgments.rationale: Nearly all participants had complete outcome data available, with only 2 patients lost to follow-up among those initiating treatment, making missing data minimal and balanced.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Among the 558 participants who initiated randomized trial treatment, 556 (99.6%) had complete follow-up at 45 days after drug initiation or at the time of trial termination, whichever came earlier, and 544 (97.5%) were followed up through day 45.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcomes were objective clinical endpoints (mortality, thromboembolism, MI, stroke, hospitalization) and were adjudicated by an independent Clinical Endpoints Committee blinded to treatment allocation.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Medical records were sent to the Clinical Endpoints Committee, who adjudicated events using standardized criteria. Both the medical monitors and the end points committee were unaware of randomized drug assignment.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was preregistered (NCT04498273), followed a prespecified statistical analysis plan, and reported all prespecified primary and secondary outcomes without evidence of selective reporting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary sample of interest for both efficacy and safety treatment comparisons was defined on an a priori basis and consisted of all randomized participants who initiated trial therapy... Details of the prespecified analysis plan are provided in the trial protocol (Supplement 1).

overall_summary: The study was a rigorously conducted, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial with central computer-generated randomization, blinded outcome adjudication, and virtually complete follow-up. All RoB 2 domains are judged to be at low risk of bias.

design_rationale: The study is a randomized, open-label, parallel-group multicentre phase 3 trial where eligible participants were randomly allocated 1:1 using a computer-generated block-stratified randomization sequence integrated into REDCap.

domain_judgments.rationale: The allocation sequence was computer-generated, concealed via central REDCap system, and baseline characteristics were well-balanced between groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The randomisation sequence was computer-generated and integrated into the electronic data capture software RedCAP (Vanderbild University, version 9.1.24). This task was done by personnel of the Clinical Trial Unit of the University Hospital Zurich. ... Participants and study personnel were aware of treatment allocation, but not of the allocation sequence.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although the trial was open-label, high treatment adherence was documented (93%), care was standardized with minimal unplanned visits differing between arms, and an intention-to-treat analysis was conducted.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The study was done as an open-label randomised trial as no enoxaparin-placebo was available during the early phases of the COVID-19 pandemic. Participants and study personnel were aware of treatment allocation, but not of the allocation sequence... Analysis of the efficacy outcomes was done in the intention-to-treat (ITT) population.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome data were available for 472 out of 475 randomized patients (>99%), indicating nearly complete follow-up that is unlikely to bias results.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The final intention-to-treat population consisted of 472 patients: 234 received enoxaparin and 238 no thromboprophylaxis... Two participants withdrew their participation in the study, whereas no follow-up data were available for one patient.

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcome of hospitalisation or death was objective and determined by non-study medical personnel, making measurement bias due to the open-label design unlikely.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary outcome was a composite of any untoward hospitalisation and all-cause death within the 30 days following randomisation. A reason for hospitalisation had to fulfil the criteria of a serious adverse event to be considered for the primary outcome. The decision to admit a patient was taken by medical personnel not involved in the study... Since all serious adverse events, including hospitalisations, were adjudicated locally and by the sponsor, who had full access to the source medical documentation, no independent adjudication of untoward hospitalisations and deaths was done.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial had a published protocol and preregistration (NCT04400799), with pre-specified interim stopping rules adhered to and all pre-specified outcomes reported.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The study was registered in ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT04400799) and has been completed... At the predefined formal interim analysis for efficacy (50% of total study population), the independent Data Safety Monitoring Board recommended early termination of the trial on the basis of predefined statistical criteria

overall_summary: The trial has low risk of bias across all RoB 2 domains, with robust central randomization and concealment, minimal missing data, objective primary outcomes assessed by independent medical personnel, and adherence to a predefined protocol and analysis plan.

design_rationale: The MICHELLE study is an open-label, multicentre, randomised controlled trial in which participants were randomly allocated (1:1) to rivaroxaban or no anticoagulation using a central web-based system.

domain_judgments.rationale: Allocation sequence was centrally generated and concealed using an automated web-based system, and baseline characteristics were well balanced between groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Randomisation was done in permuted blocks of variable size, using a central, concealed, web-based, automated randomisation system (RedCap, version 11.0.3).

domain_judgments.rationale: Despite the open-label design, adherence was very high (99%), no substantial protocol deviations or non-protocol co-interventions were described, and the primary analysis followed the intention-to-treat principle.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The MICHELLE trial was an open-label study, with no masking of investigators or patients to group allocation. ... 157 (99%) of 159 patients took the study medication up to day 35 without a discontinuation greater than 7 days

domain_judgments.rationale: A substantial proportion of patients missed protocol-mandated screening imaging for asymptomatic VTE (28% vs 43% for CT angiogram, 16% vs 26% for Doppler ultrasound), with differential missingness between groups that could affect ascertainment of the primary composite outcome.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Not every patient received CT pulmonary angiogram (45 [28%] in the active group and 69 [43%] in the control group) or Doppler ultrasound (25 [16%] in the active group and 41 [26%] in the control group).

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome assessors and members of the independent clinical events adjudication committee were blinded to treatment assignment, minimizing detection bias for the composite endpoint.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: All events were evaluated by an independent clinical events adjudication committee, including a core laboratory for image analysis, whose members were unaware of the study treatment assignment.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was prospectively registered, an analysis plan was completed prior to unblinding, and the reported outcomes match the prespecified endpoints and analysis plan.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The statistical analysis plan was completed before the end of the study and unblinding of the study results and is available in the appendix (p 27). ... This trial is registered at ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT04662684.

overall_summary: The trial was well conducted with central randomization, blinded outcome adjudication, and high adherence, but there are some concerns regarding missing outcome data due to substantial and imbalanced proportions of participants not undergoing mandatory screening imaging (Doppler ultrasound and CT pulmonary angiograms) for asymptomatic endpoints.

design_rationale: Participants were randomly assigned (1:1) to subcutaneous enoxaparin or standard of care using a computer-generated block-stratified sequence integrated into electronic data capture software.

domain_judgments.rationale: The allocation sequence was random, computer-generated, centralized via RedCAP concealing allocation prior to assignment, and baseline characteristics were balanced.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Eligible participants underwent block-stratified randomisation (by age group 50–70 vs >70 years and by study centre) in a 1:1 ratio to receive either enoxaparin or standard of care (no thromboprophylaxis). The randomisation sequence was computer-generated and integrated into the electronic data capture software RedCAP... Participants and study personnel were aware of treatment allocation, but not of the allocation sequence.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although open-label, the study evaluated the effect of assignment to intervention using an intention-to-treat analysis, and there were no deviations from intended interventions that would bias results.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Analysis of the efficacy outcomes was done in the intention-to-treat (ITT) population... The final intention-to-treat population consisted of 472 patients: 234 received enoxaparin and 238 no thromboprophylaxis.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome data were available for 472 out of 475 randomized participants (less than 1% missing), making bias due to missing outcome data negligible.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Two participants withdrew their participation in the study, whereas no follow-up data were available for one patient. The final intention-to-treat population consisted of 472 patients: 234 received enoxaparin and 238 no thromboprophylaxis.

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcome components (all-cause death and hospitalization) are objective, and decisions to hospitalize were made by medical personnel not involved in the study.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The decision to admit a patient was taken by medical personnel not involved in the study... Since all serious adverse events, including hospitalisations, were adjudicated locally and by the sponsor, who had full access to the source medical documentation, no independent adjudication of untoward hospitalisations and deaths was done.

domain_judgments.rationale: The study protocol was published, trial was pre-registered, and outcomes were analyzed according to a prespecified statistical analysis plan with predefined stopping boundaries.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The study was registered in ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT04400799) and has been completed... At the predefined formal interim analysis for efficacy (50% of total study population), the independent Data Safety Monitoring Board recommended early termination of the trial on the basis of predefined statistical criteria

overall_summary: The study was judged to have low risk of bias across all five RoB 2 domains, with robust central randomisation, minimal missing outcome data, objective primary outcomes assessed by clinicians independent of the trial, and pre-specified analysis plans.
